Playbook.name: SWIFT — Unauthorized System Change on the SWIFT Payment Server - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Persistence / Create or Modify System Process

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A system change (service install 4697/7045) occurred on a SWIFT server. SWIFT servers should have a frozen software/service set. Triage: an authorised change under the SWIFT change process, or unauthorised persistence/tampering on a payment server?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Unauthorised system changes on a SWIFT server can plant persistence or tamper with the payment application.

Assets.AssetType: SWIFT Alliance payment servers (saa*, hq-sw-app*, hq-swift*)

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security on SWIFT servers - logs-system.security-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing on SWIFT hosts (verified live: saa76dr, hq-sw-app-p, hq-swift-accs-p, saa72live, hq-swift-web-p). SWIFT servers are the highest-value payment assets - any anomaly is high priority.

Signal.Name: Unauthorized System Change on the SWIFT
Signal.Details: service install / system change on a SWIFT host.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance, not any single fact.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the SWIFT-server system change is authorised or unauthorised persistence/tampering.

Step.name: The system change on the SWIFT server
Step.Purpose: The service/change detail and installer reveal an authorised change vs attacker persistence.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4697","7045") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, event.code, winlog.event_data.ServiceName, winlog.event_data.ServiceFileName, winlog.event_data.ImagePath, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A service with a suspicious image path (temp/appdata, random name) on a SWIFT server is attacker persistence. An authorised change installs a known service under the SWIFT change process. Read the image path and installer.

Node.Condition: A suspicious service (temp path/random name) installed on the SWIFT server, or a change with no CSP change record.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised SWIFT System Change - CSP incident process, IR)

Node.Condition: An authorised change under the SWIFT change-management process.
A change by a plausible admin with no change record.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-SWIFTCHG-DETAIL to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change record; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Unauthorised persistence/tampering on a SWIFT server.

SOCAction.Item: Invoke the SWIFT CSP incident process; isolate; remove the change; review payments; open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A change without proper change control.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the SWIFT server; SWIFT anomalies are high priority.
If unauthorised, isolate per the SWIFT CSP incident process.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the SWIFT server per the CSP incident process; preserve evidence; engage the SWIFT/payments team; open IR.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce SWIFT CSP controls: restricted access, MFA/jump-host, allowlisted software, segregation from the general network.

QualityChecks.Check: SWIFT servers are in-scope for the SWIFT Customer Security Programme - treat every anomaly as high priority and involve the payments team.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unauthorised change removed per CSP; payments reviewed; IR recorded.
